stem:
Relecloud works with an external tax consultant who uses an email address at a different company. The consultant must appear in the Relecloud global address list and receive email sent to a distribution list. The consultant must not be able to sign in to Relecloud resources.

What should you create?
explanation: A mail contact represents an external person with an external email address. It is visible in the global address list, can be a distribution list member, and has no sign-in credentials. A mail user is similar but has credentials, and a guest is a B2B account that can access resources.
rationale: Correct: a mail contact has an external email address, shows up in the global address list and can be added to distribution lists, and it has no credentials, so the consultant cannot sign in.

Incorrect: a mail user also has an external address, but it has sign-in credentials in Relecloud and can be granted access to resources. Use it for external people who need to sign in with an account from your organization.
Incorrect: a guest user is a B2B account that signs in with its home identity to access resources. Use it when the consultant must collaborate in Teams or SharePoint.
Incorrect: a shared mailbox stores mail inside Relecloud for several internal users. It does not forward mail to an external address.

stem:
An admin at Tailspin Toys wants to add an external supplier as a contact so that it appears in the shared address book. The admin wants to use the Microsoft 365 admin center instead of the Exchange admin center.

Which page should the admin use to create the contact?
explanation: Mail contacts can be created and viewed in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Users > Contacts, and in the Exchange admin center under Recipients > Contacts. Contacts created in either place appear in the shared address book in Outlook.
rationale: Correct: the Contacts page under Users is where you add and manage mail contacts in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Incorrect: Guest users lists B2B guest accounts that can sign in and access resources. Use it to view or remove guests, not to create address book contacts.
Incorrect: Active teams & groups manages groups and their members. After the contact exists, you can add it to a distribution list there, but you cannot create it there.
Incorrect: Org settings holds tenant-wide service and security settings, not individual recipients.

stem:
Woodgrove Bank has hundreds of mail contacts in Exchange Online. All mail contacts whose Department is Public Relations must be hidden from the global address list. The contacts must keep receiving email that is sent to them.

Which command should you run?
explanation: Get-Contact and Set-Contact handle organization and contact information such as Department, Title or Company. Get-MailContact and Set-MailContact handle mail-related properties such as email addresses, custom attributes and whether the contact is hidden from address lists. Filtering on Department therefore uses Get-Contact, and hiding uses Set-MailContact.
rationale: Correct: Get-Contact can filter on Department, and Set-MailContact with HiddenFromAddressListsEnabled $true removes each contact from address lists while email to it still works.

Incorrect: Set-Contact changes organization information. Changing the department only relabels the contacts; they stay visible in the address book. Use Set-Contact to maintain title, company or manager.
Incorrect: Remove-MailContact deletes the contacts, so mail to them stops working. Use it when the external people should no longer be recipients at all.
Incorrect: a custom attribute only stores a value, for example for filters or address lists. Setting it to Hidden does not hide the contact. Use custom attributes to tag recipients.

stem:
Fabrikam, Inc. hires 20 short-term consultants from a partner. The consultants keep using their partner email addresses for mail, which must appear in the Fabrikam address book. They must also sign in with an account issued by Fabrikam to open a SharePoint site. They do not need Fabrikam mailboxes.

What should you create for each consultant in Exchange Online PowerShell?
choices: A mail user by running New-MailUser with -ExternalEmailAddress and -MicrosoftOnlineServicesID
A mail contact by running New-MailContact with -ExternalEmailAddress and -Name
A user mailbox by running New-Mailbox with -MicrosoftOnlineServicesID and -Password
A shared mailbox by running New-Mailbox with -Shared and -DisplayName
explanation: A mail user combines an external email address, visibility in the address book and sign-in credentials in your organization, so it can be granted permissions to resources. It needs no Exchange Online license. A mail contact has no credentials, and a user mailbox stores mail inside your organization.
rationale: Correct: New-MailUser creates an account with Fabrikam credentials (MicrosoftOnlineServicesID) whose mail goes to the partner address (ExternalEmailAddress), so the consultants can sign in to SharePoint and keep their own mailboxes.
Incorrect: a mail contact appears in the address book with the external address but has no credentials, so the consultants could not sign in. Use contacts when external people only receive email.
Incorrect: a user mailbox stores email in Exchange Online, which the consultants do not need, and it requires a license. Use it for employees who receive mail at Fabrikam.
Incorrect: a shared mailbox is accessed by several internal users and has no individual sign-in. Use it for team addresses such as support or sales.

stem:
Tailspin Toys must import 150 external contacts from .\ExternalContacts.csv into Exchange Online. The file contains Name, ExternalEmailAddress, FirstName, LastName, Company, Title and Phone. The contacts must appear in the shared address book with their company, title and phone number. The contacts must not be able to sign in.

Which three actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
explanation: Bulk contact import is a two-pass job in Exchange Online PowerShell: New-MailContact creates each contact with the mail properties, and Set-Contact then fills in organization and contact information such as company, title and phone. Set-Contact needs the contacts to exist first.
rationale: Step 1: the Exchange Online cmdlets for recipients need a connected Exchange Online PowerShell session.
Step 2: New-MailContact creates each contact with its name and external email address, which makes it visible in the shared address book.
Step 3: Set-Contact adds Company, Title and Phone to the contacts that step 2 created; it fails for contacts that do not exist yet.

Incorrect: New-MailUser creates mail users with sign-in credentials, which the requirement forbids, and it also needs a password and an internal sign-in name. Use mail users for external people who must sign in.
Incorrect: New-MgInvitation creates B2B guest accounts that can sign in and access resources. Use it to invite collaborators, not to add address book entries.

stem:
You plan how to meet the auditor requirements.

For each of the following statements, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.
choices: You can meet the requirements by creating the auditors with New-MailContact in Exchange Online PowerShell.
Each auditor needs an Exchange Online license so that the auditor appears in the global address list.
To hide the auditors from address lists when the audit ends, you run Set-Contact with -HiddenFromAddressListsEnabled $true.
explanation: Mail contacts represent external people in the address book, can be distribution list members, have no credentials and need no license. Mail-related properties, including hiding from address lists, are changed with Set-MailContact, while Set-Contact changes organization and contact information.
rationale: Yes: the auditors need an address book entry, membership of the Audit Committee distribution list and no sign-in. A mail contact created with New-MailContact provides exactly that.
No: mail contacts are not licensed objects. They appear in the global address list without any license because their mailbox is hosted elsewhere.
No: hiding from address lists is a mail-related property that is set with Set-MailContact -HiddenFromAddressListsEnabled $true. Set-Contact handles organization fields such as title and department.

stem:
An admin at Contoso, Ltd. uses Bulk create on the Users page of the Microsoft Entra admin center to add 300 internal users. The admin keeps the column headers of the downloaded CSV template unchanged.

Which values should the admin enter for every user?
choices: Name, User name and Initial password
User name, Usage location and License
Email address, Display name and Redirection URL
explanation: The Bulk create template requires only Name, User name and Initial password; the other columns are optional. The operation creates internal member accounts with the passwords from the file and does not send invitation emails, so credentials must be handed over through your own process.
rationale: Correct: these three are the only required values in the Bulk create CSV template. The file must keep the exact column names from the download.
Incorrect: usage location is optional and Bulk create has no license column. Licenses are assigned afterwards, for example with group-based licensing.
Incorrect: email address and redirection URL belong to the Bulk invite template for B2B guests. Use that template to invite external users.
Incorrect: department and manager are optional profile values. They can be included but do not make an account valid.

stem:
A group owner at Relecloud must add 400 users to a security group by using Bulk operations > Import members in the Microsoft Entra admin center.

Which value should each row of the CSV file contain?
choices: The user principal name or the object ID of the member
The display name of the member as shown in the admin center
The mail nickname of the member
The employee ID of the member
explanation: The Bulk import group members template has one required column, Member object ID or user principal name. Group owners can also bulk import members of groups they own, and failed rows are listed with the reason on the Bulk operation results page.
rationale: Correct: each row needs either the UPN, such as user@relecloud.com, or the object ID GUID, one member per row.
Incorrect: display names are not unique, so the template does not accept them for matching members.
Incorrect: the mail nickname is an alias for email and is not one of the accepted identifiers in the import template.
Incorrect: employee ID is an HR attribute and is not accepted as a member identifier in the template.

stem:
Fabrikam, Inc. has 2,500 users. A script that updates the office location of every user processes only 100 users:

```powershell
Get-MgUser | ForEach-Object { Update-MgUser -UserId $_.Id -OfficeLocation "HQ" }
```

Which parameter should you add to Get-MgUser?
explanation: Microsoft Graph returns results in pages. Without -All, Get-MgUser returns only the first page, which for users is 100 accounts. -All makes the cmdlet follow the paging links until every object is returned.
rationale: Correct: -All retrieves every page of results, so all 2,500 users are passed to Update-MgUser.
Incorrect: ConsistencyLevel eventual enables advanced queries such as $count or endsWith filters. It does not change paging, so only 100 users are still returned.
Incorrect: CountVariable stores the total count of an advanced query in a variable, together with ConsistencyLevel. It reports how many users exist but does not return them all.
Incorrect: -Property selects which properties come back for each user. It does not affect how many users are returned.

stem:
Tailspin Toys must invite 200 people from partner companies as B2B guests. Each person must receive an invitation email. The admin wants to upload a CSV file in the Microsoft Entra admin center instead of using PowerShell.

Which bulk operation should the admin use?
choices: Add multiple users in the Microsoft 365 admin center
explanation: Bulk invite creates B2B guest accounts from a CSV file and sends invitation emails. Bulk create makes internal member accounts with passwords from the file and sends no invitations, and Import members only adds existing objects to a group.
rationale: Correct: Bulk invite takes the external email addresses from the CSV file, creates guest accounts and sends each person an invitation email.
Incorrect: Bulk create creates internal member accounts with initial passwords and does not send invitation emails. Use it for new employees.
Incorrect: Import members adds existing users to a group. The partners do not exist in the directory yet.
Incorrect: Add multiple users creates licensed member accounts in your organization, not guests who sign in with their home identity. Use it for new employees with licenses.

stem:
Woodgrove Bank wants a list of all member users who have no license assigned. Guest users must not be included.

Which command should you run?
choices: Get-MgUser -Filter "assignedLicenses/`$count eq 0 and userType eq 'Member'" -ConsistencyLevel eventual -CountVariable unlicensedCount -All
explanation: Filtering on assignedLicenses/$count is an advanced query, so it needs -ConsistencyLevel eventual and a count variable. Adding userType eq 'Member' removes guests, and -All returns every page instead of the first 100 results.
rationale: Correct: the $count filter finds users without licenses, userType eq 'Member' excludes guests, and ConsistencyLevel with CountVariable makes the advanced query valid.
Incorrect: the filter is right, but without -ConsistencyLevel eventual and a count the advanced query on $count is not supported and the request fails.
Incorrect: this valid query returns all unlicensed users, including guests, which the requirement excludes. Use it when guests should be counted too.
Incorrect: Get-MgSubscribedSku shows how many licenses each subscription has and uses, not which users are unlicensed. Use it to check available units before assigning licenses.

stem:
Adatum Corporation moves its 350-person Accounting department to France. All Accounting users must get the usage location France so that licenses for that country can be assigned.

Which command should you run?
explanation: Bulk updates combine a filtered Get-MgUser with Update-MgUser in a pipeline. UsageLocation is the two-letter country code that licensing checks; -All is needed because without it only the first 100 users are returned.
rationale: Correct: the filter selects Accounting, -All returns all 350 users, and UsageLocation FR is the value that license assignment uses.
Incorrect: without -All only the first 100 Accounting users are updated, so 250 users keep the old usage location.
Incorrect: Country is a profile field for the address. It is not read by license assignment, so licenses for France still cannot be checked against the users.
Incorrect: PreferredDataLocation chooses the Multi-Geo geography for user data. Use it in Multi-Geo tenants to place mailboxes and OneDrive in a satellite geo, not for licensing.

stem:
Litware, Inc. must delete 120 cloud-only users listed by user principal name in C:\temp\leavers.csv. If a user was listed by mistake, the account must be recoverable with its data for the standard period.

Which command should you run after you connect with the User.ReadWrite.All scope?
explanation: Remove-MgUser soft-deletes a user: the account stays restorable with all its properties for 30 days, after which it is permanently deleted. Remove-MgDirectoryDeletedItem permanently deletes an object that is already soft-deleted, and nobody can restore it afterwards.
rationale: Correct: Remove-MgUser deletes each listed user, and the accounts remain in Deleted users for 30 days, so a mistake can be undone by restoring the user.

Incorrect: Remove-MgDirectoryDeletedItem permanently deletes objects from the deleted items container and takes their object ID. It cannot be undone. Use it only when data must be removed immediately.
Incorrect: disabling the accounts blocks sign-in but does not delete the users. Use it when access must stop but the account must stay, for example during an investigation.
Incorrect: revoking sessions forces users to sign in again but keeps their accounts active, so they are neither deleted nor blocked.

stem:
Relecloud is moving all Sales users from Microsoft 365 E3 to Microsoft 365 E5. You first need to remove the E3 license from every Sales user. $e3Sku contains the result of Get-MgSubscribedSku for SPE_E3, and $salesUsers contains the Sales users.

Which command should you run for each user in $salesUsers?
explanation: Set-MgUserLicense always takes both AddLicenses and RemoveLicenses. AddLicenses is a list of hashtables with a SkuId, and RemoveLicenses is an array of SKU IDs (GUIDs). Pass an empty value for the side you do not use.
rationale: Correct: an empty AddLicenses and the E3 SKU ID in RemoveLicenses unassigns E3 from the user.
Incorrect: this assigns E3 instead of removing it. Use this form to add a license with an empty RemoveLicenses array.
Incorrect: RemoveLicenses expects SKU IDs, not the SkuPartNumber string SPE_E3, so the license is not removed.
Incorrect: usage location is required to assign licenses, and clearing it does not remove an assigned license. Use Update-MgUser to set usage location before licensing.

stem:
Contoso, Ltd. receives C:\temp\NewAccounts.csv with DisplayName, UserPrincipalName, MailNickname and UsageLocation for 250 new employees. With Microsoft Graph PowerShell, you must create the cloud-only accounts, assign each one a Microsoft 365 E5 license (SPE_E5), and then confirm that no member account is left without a license.

Which four actions should you perform in sequence? To answer, move the appropriate actions from the list of actions to the answer area and arrange them in the correct order.
choices: For each CSV row: `$u = New-MgUser` with `-UsageLocation`, `-PasswordProfile` and `-AccountEnabled`, followed by `Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $u.Id -AddLicenses @{SkuId = $sku.SkuId} -RemoveLicenses @()`
`Get-MgUser -Filter "assignedLicenses/`$count eq 0 and userType eq 'Member'" -ConsistencyLevel eventual -CountVariable unlicensedCount -All`
explanation: A bulk provisioning script connects with scopes to write users and read subscriptions, resolves the SKU ID once, then creates each user with a usage location and licenses it in the same loop. An advanced $count query at the end proves that nobody was missed.
rationale: Step 1: User.ReadWrite.All creates users and assigns licenses, and Organization.Read.All reads the subscribed SKUs.
Step 2: the loop uses $sku.SkuId, so the E5 SKU must be resolved before any license is assigned.
Step 3: each user is created with a usage location, which licensing requires, and the returned $u.Id is licensed right away.
Step 4: the advanced query with $count, ConsistencyLevel and CountVariable lists member users without licenses, which should return none.
Incorrect: Connect-MsolService belongs to the retired MSOnline module. Use Connect-MgGraph from Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
Incorrect: New-MgInvitation creates B2B guest accounts for external people. The new employees need internal member accounts.

stem:
Tailspin Toys must assign a Microsoft 365 E5 license to every user in the Sales department, about 600 users, who all work in the United Kingdom.

How should you complete the script? To answer, select the appropriate options in the answer area.

```powershell
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "User.ReadWrite.All","Organization.Read.All"
$sku = [[1]] | Where SkuPartNumber -eq 'SPE_E5'
$users = Get-MgUser -Filter "department eq 'Sales'" [[2]]
foreach ($u in $users) {
  Update-MgUser -UserId $u.Id -UsageLocation "GB"
  Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $u.Id -AddLicenses [[3]] -RemoveLicenses @()
}
```

targets.label: Box 1
why: Correct: Get-MgSubscribedSku lists the licensing plans of the tenant, including SkuPartNumber and SkuId, so the E5 SKU can be found.
Incorrect: Get-MgUserLicenseDetail shows the licenses already assigned to one user, and $u is not defined yet at this point. Use it to check a user's current licenses.
Incorrect: Get-MgOrganization returns tenant properties such as verified domains, not the subscribed SKUs with their SKU IDs.

targets.label: Box 2
why: Correct: -All follows every page of results, so all 600 Sales users are returned.
Incorrect: -Top 100 limits the result to 100 users, so 500 users would get no license. Use -Top to sample results.
Incorrect: CountVariable stores a count for advanced queries with ConsistencyLevel; it does not return every page of users.

targets.label: Box 3
why: Correct: AddLicenses expects hashtables with a SkuId key that holds the GUID of the SKU.
Incorrect: SkuPartNumber is the readable name SPE_E5, not the GUID that SkuId requires, so the assignment fails.
Incorrect: a plain array of GUIDs is the format for RemoveLicenses. AddLicenses needs hashtables, optionally with disabled plans.

explanation: To license users in bulk, resolve the SKU ID with Get-MgSubscribedSku, retrieve all target users with -All, set a usage location, and pass @{SkuId = ...} to AddLicenses with an empty RemoveLicenses array.

stem:
Fabrikam, Inc. has no on-premises Active Directory. You must create 500 cloud-only member accounts from a CSV file that contains the name, user name and initial password of each employee. No invitation emails must be sent.

Which two methods should you use? Each correct answer presents a complete solution.
choices: Bulk create on the Users page of the Microsoft Entra admin center
A Microsoft Graph PowerShell script that runs Import-Csv and New-MgUser for each row
Bulk invite on the Users page of the Microsoft Entra admin center
A Microsoft Graph PowerShell script that runs Import-Csv and New-MgInvitation for each row
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync with a filter on the organizational unit of the employees
explanation: Internal member accounts with passwords from a file can be created in the portal with Bulk create or in PowerShell with New-MgUser in a loop. Invitations create guests, and Microsoft Entra Connect Sync needs an on-premises directory as the source.
rationale: Correct: Bulk create imports the CSV template with name, user name and initial password, creates member accounts and sends no invitation emails.

Correct: a script that reads the CSV and calls New-MgUser with a PasswordProfile creates the same cloud-only member accounts without invitations. It also handles large tenants where portal bulk jobs time out.
Incorrect: Bulk invite creates B2B guest accounts and sends invitation emails, which breaks both requirements. Use it for partners.
Incorrect: New-MgInvitation also creates guests and is meant for external people. Use it for scripted bulk guest invitations.
Incorrect: Microsoft Entra Connect Sync synchronizes accounts from on-premises Active Directory, which Fabrikam does not have, and the accounts would not be cloud-only.
